title: Space Tech Briefing — July 28, 2026
summary:
Good morning, space enthusiasts! This is your daily dose of the cosmos, live from the Space Technology Desk. I'm your host, ready to blast off into the latest headlines on this fantastic Tuesday, July 28, 2026. We've got groundbreaking discoveries, a chance to test your cosmic smarts, and a look back at a monumental recent flight!

First up, a truly mind-bending revelation from the European Space Agency! The Euclid space telescope has just made an incredible find, detecting no fewer than 31 of the most ancient quasars ever observed. This isn't just a number; it's a direct window into the very first phases of our universe. Euclid is allowing us to trace back the formation of galaxies and the supermassive black holes at their hearts, giving us unprecedented insights into cosmic dawn. What an achievement for understanding our universe's origins!

Next, for all you armchair astronauts and aspiring astrophysicists, how well do you *really* know our home star? The French space agency CNES recently launched a special quiz to test your knowledge of the Sun and its intricate dance with the Earth-Moon system, especially concerning solar eclipses. It’s a fantastic way to challenge yourself and deepen your understanding of the celestial mechanics right in our own backyard. Go test your solar savvy!

And now, as we wait for today's new launches, let's look back at a major recent development that has everyone talking. Just a few days ago, on July 24th UTC, SpaceX successfully completed Starship Flight 13! This thirteenth test flight marked a truly significant milestone for the Starship program. It wasn't just a launch; it was a full demonstration of critical technical objectives. We saw the successful deployment of the very first Starlink V3 satellites, a crucial in-flight engine relight, and a precise atmospheric re-entry of the upper stage, culminating in a gentle splashdown in the Indian Ocean. This flight officially validated the Raptor V3 engines in space, setting the stage for what many are hoping will be Starship's first orbital mission on Flight 14. An incredible step forward for humanity's multi-planetary future!

That's all for your morning briefing from the Space Technology Desk. Thank you for joining me on this journey through the latest in space. Stay curious, keep looking up, and have a stellar day!
